title: Temporal Entanglement from Twist Correlators in 2d Conformal Field Theory and Holography
authors: Alice Bernamonti, Federico Galli, Michal P. Heller, Fabio Ori, Alexandre Serantes
abstract: We formulate timelike entanglement entropy and its Rényi extension in two-dimensional conformal field theory through the analytic continuation of replica twist correlators to time-ordered, timelike-separated insertions. This field-theoretic construction grounds and generalizes recent developments, and applies to temporal subregions of arbitrary extent. Within three-dimensional holography, the semiclassical boundary correlator identifies boundary-anchored complex geodesics as the relevant bulk saddles and selects the one with the smallest real part of the length. This provides a direct boundary derivation of the proposed complex extremal surface prescription and extends to Rényi index $n>1$, for which we explicitly construct the corresponding complex cosmic brane geometry in the vacuum. We develop these ideas in several representative settings, including locally and globally excited states and quantum operator quenches, making manifest the precise agreement between boundary twist correlator and bulk complex geodesic calculations. For AdS-Vaidya, our approach predicts a different result from earlier piecewise geodesic constructions, while reproducing the field theory answer. Across these examples, the operator ordering uniquely determines the imaginary part of the complex-valued entropy, which is quantized in units of $cπ/6$ and sensitive to the effective causal structure but not to the underlying dynamics.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous framework to calculate temporal entanglement entropy in 2D CFTs by analytically continuing replica twist correlators from Euclidean to Lorentzian time. Holographically, this translates into finding complex geodesics in AdS space that match the field theory results across various physical quenches and states.
main_problem: The primary goal is formulating and calculating timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) and its Rényi extension in 2D Conformal Field Theory (CFT) and establishing its holographic dual description.
main_result: The authors provide a systematic field-theoretic construction using analytic continuation of replica twist correlators, which yields explicit agreement with complex geodesic calculations in holography for various physical scenarios.
method: The methodology involves analytically continuing Euclidean replica twist correlators to time-ordered, timelike-separated insertions in CFT. Holographically, this translates to identifying and selecting specific complex geodesics in the bulk AdS geometry that minimize the real part of their length.
model_or_system: The work applies to 2D CFTs considering temporal subregions of arbitrary extent, with holographic duals modeled by Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, including specific backgrounds like AdS-Vaidya geometry. The analysis covers quantum operator quenches and excited states.
key_observables: Timelike Entanglement Entropy ($S(T)$), Rényi entanglement entropy, complex-valued entropies (pseudoentropies), and the imaginary part of the entropy.
important_parameters: Rényi index $n$, time separation $\Delta t$, and parameters defining the specific AdS background geometry.
main_assumptions: The approach relies on analytic continuation from Euclidean to Lorentzian signature and utilizes a geodesic approximation in the bulk spacetime, which is necessary because no real geodesic connects timelike-separated points on the boundary.
figures_summary: Figure 11 (referenced in notes) compares numerical solutions for correlators against analytical forms derived from AdS and BTZ geometries, demonstrating consistency under specific limiting procedures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the field-theoretic definition of TEE via replica twist correlators, extends this to Rényi indices $n>1$, derives the corresponding complex extremal surface prescription in holography, and validates these results across multiple physical examples like quenches and excited states.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful extension of entanglement concepts into time-dependent regimes (Lorentzian signature), which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly coupled quantum systems relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems.
